video.title: If this, then that: Decisions, AND and OR
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Code is typed out on a card, left to right in both languages. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor — the students’ science teacher (main character)
Ms Amina Bello — the students’ teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice, talking to the student (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.narration: Our classroom fan was on all night, with nobody in the room! A fan needs to decide. Is it hot, and is someone here?
Today: decisions. If this, then that.
A decision starts with if. If it is raining, then take an umbrella. The if part is a question: is it raining? The answer is yes or no.
Else tells the robot what to do when the answer is no. If the light is red, stop. Else, if it isn’t red, go. Every if is a fork in the road.
Some decisions ask two questions. The fan goes on if it is hot AND someone is in the room. Both must be yes. With OR, one yes is enough.

Decisions are everywhere. A street light: if it is dark, switch on. A game: if a player who isn’t the goalkeeper touches the ball with their hand on purpose, it’s a free kick. Your phone: if the battery is low, show a warning.
Quick check! The rule is: fan on if it is hot AND someone is in. It is hot, but the room is empty. Does the fan go on?
No. AND needs both answers to be yes, and nobody is in the room. That saves electricity all night!
In the app, open Logic gates. Flip the switches and watch the lamp. Then solve the Fan puzzle: test every row until all of them are right.
Your turn. The alarm rings if the door OR the window opens. Only the window opens. Does it ring?
Yes, it rings. Remember: if asks a yes or no question. Else says what to do when the answer is no. AND needs both; OR needs one.
Try it yourself: play If this, then that with your family. One person says a rule, like: if you are wearing blue, stand up. Everyone checks the rule, and does it only if it’s true.

checkpoints.prompt: Fan on if hot AND someone is in. It is hot, but the room is empty. Does the fan go on?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — AND needs both. The room is empty, so the fan stays off.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — with AND, both must be yes. Nobody is in, so it stays off.

checkpoints.prompt: The alarm rings if the door OR the window opens. Only the window opens. Does it ring?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — with OR, one yes is enough.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — OR needs only one yes, and the window opened.
